children: Volvo Car said it is making its largest-ever product push, launching 13 new car models by the end of the decade in an effort to revive its fortunes.

The Swedish carmaker--which is majority-owned by China's Zhejiang Geely Holding Group--on Thursday laid out its roadmap to navigate a tough auto market and deliver on its long-term goals of driving sales growth and higher profitability.

Faced with U.S. tariffs on one side and pricing pressures due to the rise of the Chinese car industry on the other, Volvo initially turned to cost-cutting to protect profitability. The company said it is now embarking on a product offensive, as it pushes ahead with plans to bring down costs.
Volvo said it would roll out seven new car models for Western markets and six for China by 2030. It currently sells 14 models, with different variants of each.
The company aims to double its market share through a regionalized portfolio with electrified and all-electric cars, as well as a new generation of hybrid models, it said.

Volvo Chief Executive Officer Hakan Samuelsson said the auto industry is grappling with challenges stemming from its electrification shift, the end of globalization and heightened competition amid Chinese carmakers' international expansion.

The automaker said its renewed model lineup would be a key lever in its efforts to drive strong growth and cash flows over the long term, as well as an operating profit margin--a key profitability metric in the industry--above 8%.

The company said its new models for Western markets would use existing computing platforms and car architectures, allowing investments in its technology stack and manufacturing to decline from current levels.
In China, Volvo will work together with Geely on shared platforms and supply chains to boost efficiency, it added.
